The specification is for Spring XD (eXtreme Data), which is a framework for data pipelines. The user stories are:

U1: Migration from 1.0 to 1.1, including porting custom modules
U2: Pig script/job sample as reference
U3: Build XD on Windows machine
U4: Run acceptance test coverage in Windows (provision Windows image in EC2)
U5: Build Spark Streaming as data processors (Java/Lambdas and Scala)
U6: Update copyright message in reference guide PDF (2014 → 2015)
U7: Upgrade to Kafka's SI GA release (backport Kafka XD changes to SI Kafka, then upgrade to GA)
U8: Upgrade to SHDP GA release

1. U1 - Migration guide from 1.0 to 1.1
   - Analyze breaking changes between 1.0 and 1.1
   - Write migration guide documentation
   - Document custom module porting process
   - Test migration steps

2. U2 - Pig script/job sample
   - Design Pig integration with XD
   - Create sample Pig script
   - Create sample XD configuration for Pig job
   - Write documentation

3. U3 - Build XD on Windows
   - Investigate Windows-specific build issues
   - Fix build script issues
   - Test full build on Windows
   - Update CI scripts if needed

4. U4 - Windows acceptance test in EC2
   - Set up Windows EC2 image
   - Configure acceptance test environment
   - Adapt acceptance tests to run on Windows
   - Create CI build configuration for Windows

5. U5 - Spark Streaming as data processors
   - Design Spark Streaming integration
   - Implement Java/Lambda version
   - Implement Scala version
   - Write tests
   - Documentation

6. U6 - Update copyright
   - Simple documentation update

7. U7 - Upgrade to Kafka SI GA release
   - Backport Kafka XD changes to SI Kafka
   - Upgrade to GA release
   - Test integration
   - Update documentation

8. U8 - Upgrade to SHDP GA release
   - Update dependencies
   - Test integration
   - Update documentation

Now let me think about realistic effort estimates for an experienced developer:

1. U1 - Migration documentation and module porting guide
   - Analysis of breaking changes: 2 days
   - Writing migration guide: 3 days
   - Testing migration with sample modules: 2 days
   - Subtotal: 7 days

2. U2 - Pig sample
   - Create sample Pig script: 1 day
   - Create XD integration config: 1 day
   - Documentation: 1 day
   - Subtotal: 3 days

3. U3 - Windows build support
   - Investigate and fix Windows build issues: 3 days
   - Test full Windows build: 1 day
   - Subtotal: 4 days

4. U4 - Windows acceptance test in EC2
   - Provision Windows EC2 image: 1 day
   - Adapt tests for Windows: 2 days
   - Set up CI: 2 days
   - Subtotal: 5 days

5. U5 - Spark Streaming integration
   - Design integration: 2 days
   - Java implementation: 5 days
   - Scala implementation: 3 days
   - Testing: 3 days
   - Documentation: 2 days
   - Subtotal: 15 days

6. U6 - Copyright update
   - 0.5 days

7. U7 - Kafka SI upgrade
   - Analyze differences and backport: 3 days
   - Upgrade to GA release: 2 days
   - Test integration: 2 days
   - Documentation: 1 day
   - Subtotal: 8 days

8. U8 - SHDP upgrade
   - Update dependencies: 1 day
   - Test integration: 1 day
   - Documentation: 0.5 days
   - Subtotal: 2.5 days

Total: 7 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 15 + 0.5 + 8 + 2.5 = 45 days

technical_and_design_decisions: Migration guide (U1) is delivered as Markdown/Asciidoctor source that feeds into the same reference guide pipeline as the rest of the XD docs.
The Pig sample (U2) will be implemented as a 'pigjob' module type, consistent with existing XD processor/source/sink abstractions.
Windows build fixes (U3) target Windows Server 2012/2014 with 64-bit JDK 8, assuming the toolchain (Gradle, Git, etc.) is already installed by the build script.
Windows acceptance tests in EC2 (U4) will use a pre-baked Windows Server AMI with all prerequisites; the CI build will be implemented as a separate Jenkins job (not cross-platform Gradle).

Spark Streaming integration (U5) will reuse the existing XD processor module SPI; Java implementation will use Java 8 Lambdas and the Scala implementation will be a thin wrapper around the Java API to avoid duplication.
Kafka SI upgrade (U7) assumes the backport effort is limited to a known set of XD-specific Kafka consumer/producer extensions, not a full feature rewrite.
SHDP (U8) is treated as a dependency-only upgrade (no API changes expected), with minor configuration adjustments.
All documentation updates will flow through the existing Asciidoctor-based reference guide generation pipeline.
assumptions: The developer is experienced with Spring XD internals, Gradle builds, and the Kafka/Spark ecosystems.
A single developer performs all activities (no parallel work or specialized roles).
XD 1.1 codebase is already checked out and buildable on Linux prior to starting work.
The Spring IO platform (SI) Kafka and SHDP GA artifacts are available in Maven Central at the time of work.
Test infrastructure (Kafka, ZooKeeper, YARN) is pre-existing in the dev environment.
Effort estimates include coding, local testing, and writing/ updating documentation, but exclude code review, meetings, and CI infrastructure maintenance beyond initial setup.
Unit tests are written alongside implementation; full integration/acceptance test runs are charged only when explicitly part of the story (e.g., U4).
A workday equals 8 hours of focused development effort.

activities.activity_description: Review the 1.0→1.1 changelog, diff public APIs, identify breaking configuration changes, and list the items users must address when migrating.
Author the step-by-step migration guide covering CLI, server, modules, configuration, and known incompatibilities.
Describe how to recompile/repackage custom modules against the 1.1 module SPI, with worked examples.
Apply the documented migration steps to one or two representative custom modules to confirm the guide is accurate.
Decide module type, parameter mapping, and how Pig scripts are submitted/executed from an XD stream.
Write a representative, well-commented Pig Latin script suitable as a reference.

activities.activity_name: Create sample XD configuration for Pig
activities.activity_description: Provide stream definitions (e.g., file → pigjob → log) and any required module jars.
Write a short 'Getting Started with Pig in XD' section, including prerequisites and how to run the sample.
Install/configure JDK, Gradle, and any required Windows tooling on a Windows dev machine.
Diagnose and patch path, line-ending, shell, and native-binary issues that prevent the Gradle build from completing on Windows.
Run a clean build and the standard test suite on Windows to confirm parity with Linux.
Create/configure a Windows Server AMI with JDK, Git, and XD prerequisites installed.

activities.activity_name: Configure acceptance test environment on Windows
activities.activity_description: Install XD, prepare test data, and configure the acceptance-test runner on the Windows instance.
Adjust shell scripts, path handling, and process-management assumptions so the existing acceptance tests pass on Windows.
Create a Jenkins job (or equivalent) that launches the Windows EC2 instance, runs the adapted acceptance tests, and reports results.
Define how Spark Streaming jobs map to XD processors, including receiver/DStream lifecycle, checkpointing, and deployment modes (local/cluster).
Build the processor implementation and supporting SPI in Java, using Java 8 Lambdas where appropriate.
Provide a Scala-flavored processor that demonstrates idiomatic Scala usage and reuses the Java implementation where reasonable.

activities.activity_name: Write tests for Spark Streaming processors
activities.activity_description: Unit tests with a local SparkContext and at least one integration test against a running Spark cluster.
Add a 'Spark Streaming' chapter to the reference guide with configuration options, examples, and limitations.

activities.activity_name: Update copyright year in reference guide
activities.activity_description: Change the 2014 copyright notice to 2015 in the Asciidoctor source and regenerate the PDF.

activities.activity_name: Analyze SI Kafka vs XD Kafka differences
activities.activity_description: Diff the XD Kafka adapter against the current SI Kafka adapter to enumerate required backports.

activities.activity_name: Backport XD Kafka changes to SI Kafka
activities.activity_description: Port XD-specific Kafka extensions (codecs, partition selectors, etc.) onto the SI Kafka codebase.

activities.activity_name: Upgrade SI Kafka dependency to GA release
activities.activity_description: Bump the version in the build, resolve any API/dependency changes, and recompile affected modules.
Run the Kafka source/processor/sink integration tests against a real broker to verify end-to-end behavior.
Reflect the new Kafka GA version and any configuration changes in the reference guide.

activities.activity_name: Update SHDP dependency to GA release
activities.activity_description: Change the SHDP version in the Gradle build and resolve any transitive dependency conflicts.
Run the SHDP-related integration tests (HDFS, YARN) to confirm nothing regressed.
Update version references and any new configuration options in the reference guide.
